 HARTFORD, CT — On the morning after what he called a tidal wave election that swept Democrats into power nationally and expanded the party’s state dominance , Gov. Ned Lamont laid out his priorities for the upcoming term, and said the results would not change his governing style.
 “Big table, open door, and I welcome progressives, moderates, Republicans, come in and give me your best idea. But make it real,” he said. “Today, elections are over. It’s not about campaign promises, it’s what you’re actually able to deliver.”
 Lamont said early discussions on the next budget already had begun.
 “I feel pretty good that the state is in better fiscal shape than it’s been in many years,” he said. “I think that means that we do have some resources, that we’re able to do some big things.”
 Specifically Lamont cited the Early Childhood Endowment Fund, which he said the state would be able to add to in the current budget cycle. Other priorities included healthcare costs.
 “I know what that’s doing to small businesses. I know what that’s doing to not-for-profits. I know what that’s doing to our state budget,” he said. “There we can go into what we meant by the Connecticut option. I hope that’s on the offense, where we’ll be able to expand healthcare and make it affordable for everybody.”
 Toward that end, Lamont again mentioned his proposal to assess large corporations for every employee of theirs on Medicaid for their health coverage.
 Finally, Lamont talked about education, saying he hoped to present a plan to regionalize services institute an insurance cap and other measures he said could reduce costs.
 “I don’t just want more money for the status quo, but I like to show that we can make a big difference with the monies we do invest,” he said.
 Lamont, in response to a question about Republican losses in the state Senate, said he wanted the now-diminished Republican caucus participating in the budget process.
 “I want them at the table. I want them to be constructive,” he said. “Don’t tell me what you don’t like, tell me what you do like. And tell me how we can get there together. That’s how you’re relevant.”
